hindi: “तुम और मैं दुर्ग बनवाते हैं।” यह कर्म-सन्धि है।
english: "You and I have a fort built." Such is the treaty of works.
notes: Closing iti + label: glossary pattern 'Such is X'. karma-sandhi: karma rendered 'works' (the joint undertaking, building a fort; glossary 7.1/7.3 'works' for the king's undertakings); sandhi = treaty (Book 7). The present kārayāvahe is a proposal (let us two have a fort built); rendered literally. The dual verb is not separately expressed in the translation.

hindi: उन दोनों में से जो दैव द्वारा किया हुआ, असह्य, जिसके आरम्भ में थोड़ा व्यय है ऐसा दुर्ग बनवाता है, वह छल लेता है।
english: Of those two, he who has a fort built that is made by the divine, unbearable, [and] whose undertaking has little expenditure — he outwits [the other].
notes: daiva-kṛta = made by the divine (a natural fort); aviṣahya 'unbearable' (alternatives: unassailable, that cannot be withstood). The object of atisandhatte is not stated; supplied in brackets in English only.

words.gloss: of land, river and mountain forts

hindi: वहाँ भी स्थल, नदी, पर्वत के दुर्गों में आगे-आगे वाला बेहतर।
english: There too, of land, river and mountain forts, each succeeding [one is] better.
notes: Verbless; the copula is supplied (bracketed in English).

words.gloss: than [one] with water to be brought

hindi: दो सेतु-बन्धों में भी जलयुक्त वाला, लाए जाने योग्य जल वाले से बेहतर।
english: Of two embankment-dams too, [the one] with water [is] better than [the one] with water to be brought.
notes: setu-bandha is the glossary compound (3.9) 'embankment-dam' taken as one item, the dual ending giving 'two embankment-dams'; the alternative is 'of embankment and dam' (two items). saha-udaka read as 'having water (of its own)' against water that must be brought; the Sanskrit does not say 'own'. Case of -ayoḥ (gen. or loc.) is ambiguous.

hindi: जलयुक्त दो में भी बोने के प्रचुर स्थानों वाला बेहतर।
english: Of two having water too, [the one] with abundant places for sowing [is] better.
notes: vāpa = sowing (√vap); sthāna = place. The exact sense of vāpa-sthāna is not certain (alternatives: room for sowing, planting-ground).

words.gloss: having forest-wilds of great, valuable produce
at the end of the territory

hindi: दो द्रव्य-वनों में भी जो देश के अन्त में, बड़े सारवान् द्रव्य के जंगलों वाले, नदी-मातृक द्रव्य-वन को कटवाता है, वह छल लेता है।
english: Of two produce-forests too, he who has cut a produce-forest that has forest-wilds of great, valuable produce, at the end of the territory, [and] river-mothered — he outwits [the other].
notes: dravya-vana = produce-forest (glossary 7.1, members literal; dravya = produce, alternatives: material, timber; sense not settled). aṭavīka read as 'having aṭavī (forest-wilds)' with the suffix -ka; the force sense of aṭavī (forest tribes, 8.1) is not taken. nadī-mātṛka literally 'having the river as mother'; the usual sense (watered by a river rather than by rain) is an interpretation and is kept out of the translation. chedayati is causative, 'has cut'. The object of atisandhatte is supplied in brackets in English only.

hindi: क्योंकि नदी-मातृक सुजीविका है और आपत्ति में आश्रय है।
english: For [what is] river-mothered is a good livelihood, and a refuge in adversity.
notes: The subject is the river-mothered produce-forest of unit 6, not repeated here; nothing is supplied in Hindi. sv.ājīvam = su-ājīvam by regular sandhi (not a typo). apāśraya = refuge, support. Gender mix (n. subject, m. predicate) is normal for a predicate noun.

words.gloss: at the end of the territory

hindi: दो हाथी-वनों में भी जो देश के अन्त में, बहुत शूर पशुओं वाले, दुर्बल पड़ोसियों वाले, अनन्त-अवक्लेशी हाथी-वन को बाँधता है, वह छल लेता है।
english: Of two elephant-forests too, he who binds an elephant-forest at the end of the territory, having many brave animals, having weak neighbours, [and] ananta-avakleśin — he outwits [the other].

text_flags.why: possible: the compound dot after the final anusvāra of prativeśam joins two separate words; a space is expected (two adjectives of hasti-vanam)

notes: ananta-avakleśin is obscure (ananta 'endless'; avakleśin from ava-√kliś, 'troubling/afflicting'); kept untranslated in the translations, no sense guessed (the sense could be favourable or unfavourable). badhnāti = 'binds' (the sense 'secures/reserves' is an interpretation). mṛga = animal; here presumably elephants, but not stated.

words.gloss: of [the two] with many blunt and with few brave
words.gram: dvandva of bahuvrīhis; n. gen./loc. du.

hindi: वहाँ भी — “बहुत भोथरे और थोड़े शूर वाले दोनों में थोड़े शूर वाला बेहतर, क्योंकि युद्ध शूरों में है; थोड़े शूर बहुत-से अशूरों को तोड़ते हैं; वे टूटे हुए अपनी सेना को मारने वाले बन जाते हैं,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: There too — "Of [the two] with many blunt [ones] and with few brave [ones], [the one] with few brave [ones is] better, for battle [is] among the brave; few brave [ones] break many non-brave ones; those, broken, become strikers-down of their own army," say the teachers.
notes: kuṇṭha = blunt (here of troops or animals; the unit follows the elephant-forest unit 8, so 'animals' is possible; not stated). The dual compound is a dvandva of two bahuvrīhis. Quotation opened in this unit (the teachers' view), closed by iti (rendered by the closing mark only). śūrā = śūrāḥ (visarga dropped before b).

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: "No," says Kautilya.
notes: na-iti is an unsandhied join of two words; glossary formula.

words.gram: pres. mid. part. √kṛ; m. nom. pl.

hindi: “बहुत भोथरे बेहतरं; टुकड़ी में लगाए जाने से अनेक कर्म करते हुए, युद्ध में अपनों के आश्रय, और दूसरों के लिए दुर्धर्ष और भयंकर।
english: "The blunt [ones], the many, [are] better: doing action of many kinds through assignment to the contingent, [they are] a refuge to their own in battle, and hard to overcome and frightening to the others.
notes: Kautilya's reply (after na-iti kauṭilyaḥ) is read as a quotation running over units 11-12, closed by the iti of unit 12; the opening mark is placed here, no text_flag. skandha = contingent (lit. shoulder, trunk; glossary 12.3 'frontier contingent'); the sense is uncertain (alternatives: main body, mass). karma here is action in the general sense (troops' conduct), not the 7.1 'works' of undertakings. kuṇṭhā = kuṇṭhāḥ and durdharṣā = durdharṣāḥ (visarga dropped before b/v). pareṣām = 'of the others', not 'enemies' (glossary 9.2). The second part may also be read with ca joining durdharṣāḥ and vibhīṣaṇāḥ (as done).

hindi: क्योंकि बहुत भोथरों में विनय-कर्म से शूरता डाली जा सकती है; किन्तु थोड़े शूरों में बहुत्व नहीं ही।”
english: For among many blunt [ones], valour can be put in by discipline-action; but certainly not numerousness among few brave [ones]."
notes: Closes the quotation opened in unit 11 (iti rendered by the closing mark only). 'na tu eva' is rendered word by word (not, but, certainly), a possible idiom 'but by no means'; the predicate (śakyam) is understood. vinaya-karman = action of discipline (training). ādhātum literally 'to place in'.

hindi: दो खानों में भी जो प्रचुर बहुमूल्य वस्तुओं वाली, जिसके मार्ग दुर्गम नहीं हैं ऐसी, जिसके आरम्भ में थोड़ा व्यय है ऐसी खान खुदवाता है, वह छल लेता है।
english: Of two mines too, he who has a mine dug that has abundant valuables, roads not difficult, [and] an undertaking of little expenditure — he outwits [the other].
notes: adurga-mārga: durga here read as 'difficult' (a-durga = not difficult); the alternative is durga = fort ('without a fort on the road'). sāra = valuables (glossary). The object of atisandhatte is supplied in English only.

words.gloss: mineral of diamond, gem, pearl, coral, gold, silver

hindi: वहाँ भी — बड़ी बहुमूल्य वस्तुओं वाला थोड़ा, अथवा थोड़ी बहुमूल्य वस्तुओं वाला प्रचुर — “बड़ी बहुमूल्य वस्तुओं वाला थोड़ा बेहतर; क्योंकि वज्र, मणि, मोती, मूँगा, सोना, चाँदी का धातु प्रचुर, थोड़ी बहुमूल्य वस्तुओं वाले को अति ऊँचे मूल्य से निगल लेता है,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: There too — [a mine] of great valuables [but] small, or of few valuables [but] abundant — "[One] of great valuables [but] small is better; for the mineral of diamond, gem, pearl, coral, gold and silver swallows [one] abundant [but] of few valuables by [its] very high price," say the teachers.
notes: The first iti closes the statement of the two alternatives (not rendered; carried by the dashes); no noun is stated, 'a mine' is understood from unit 13 and bracketed in English only. dhātu = mineral (alternatives: metal, ore, element); the compound lists diamond, gem, pearl, coral, gold (hema), silver (rūpya) with dhātu; the exact structure is uncertain. grasate 'swallows' is figurative (outweighs by price) but is rendered literally. Quotation closed by the second iti.

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: "No," says Kautilya.
notes: na-iti is an unsandhied join of two words; glossary formula.

hindi: देर से बड़ी बहुमूल्य वस्तुओं वाले का थोड़ा क्रेता मिलता है; निरन्तरता से थोड़ी बहुमूल्य वस्तुओं वाले का प्रचुर।
english: After a long time a scanty buyer of [one] of great valuables is found; [a buyer] abundant, from continuity, of [one] of few valuables.
notes: alpaḥ kretā: a singular used collectively, 'scanty' = few; prabhūtaḥ likewise, with kretā and vidyate understood (English brackets only; Hindi left verbless). The noun to which mahā-sāra / alpa-sāra refers (mine or its produce) is not stated.

hindi: इससे वणिक्-पथ की व्याख्या की गई।
english: By this the merchant route is explained.
notes: Glossary formula 'tena X vyākhyātam'. patha rendered 'route' throughout this chunk.

words.gloss: of water route and land route

hindi: वहाँ भी — “जल-मार्ग और स्थल-मार्ग में जल-मार्ग बेहतर, थोड़े व्यय और व्यायाम वाला और पण्य का प्रचुर उदय वाला,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: There too — "Of the water route and the land route, the water route [is] better, with little expenditure and exertion, and with abundant rise of wares," say the teachers.
notes: vyāyāma = exertion (glossary 10.4 sense; not 6.2 'activity'). udaya = rise (3.12 'increase'). The alpa- prefix is read as governing both vyaya and vyāyāma.

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: "No," says Kautilya.
notes: na-iti is an unsandhied join of two words; glossary formula.

hindi: जल-मार्ग अवरुद्ध गति वाला, सब समय का नहीं, प्रबल भय का स्रोत और प्रतिकार-रहित है; स्थल-मार्ग विपरीत है।
english: The water route [is] of obstructed movement, not of all times, a source of great fear, and without remedy; the land route [is] the opposite.
notes: The e-text spells samruddha (and samyāna in unit 21) with m before r/y, a habit of this e-text (both spellings occur throughout); w gives the standard saṃ-; not flagged. asārvakālika: 'not [available] at all times' (alternative: not of every season). pratīkāra = remedy (glossary).

words.gloss: of shore route and saṃyāna route

hindi: किन्तु जल-मार्ग में कूल-संयान-मार्गों में से कूल-मार्ग पण्य-पत्तनों की बहुलता के कारण बेहतर, अथवा नदी-मार्ग, निरन्तरता के कारण और सहने योग्य बाधा होने के कारण।
english: But in the water route, of the shore route and the saṃyāna route, the shore route [is] better because of the abundance of ware-towns, or the river route, because of continuity and because of [its] bearable hindrance.
notes: saṃyāna is obscure here (sam-√yā, going together/voyage) and kept untranslated; the dual -pathayoḥ makes it a pair with kūla. paṇya-pattana: 'ware-towns' (alternative: wares and towns/ports). viṣahya-ābādha: viṣahya = bearable (gerundive), ābādha = hindrance/trouble. 'vā' offers the river route as an alternative; the e-text writes samyāna for saṃyāna (see unit 20 note).

words.gloss: wares of elephants, horses, scents, tusks, hides, silver, gold

hindi: स्थल-मार्ग में भी — “हैमवत, दक्षिणापथ से बेहतर; हाथी, घोड़े, गन्ध, दाँत, खाल, चाँदी, सोने के पण्य अधिक बहुमूल्य हैं,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: In the land route too — "The Himalayan [route is] better than the southern route; [its] wares of elephants, horses, scents, tusks, hides, silver [and] gold [are] more valuable," say the teachers.

text_flags.why: stray closing quotation mark: the quotation already closes after sāravattarāḥ and iti follows

notes: haimavata: the route is not named in the Sanskrit ('route' is bracketed in English); dakṣiṇā-patha = southern route (the usual name is Dakshinapatha; not imported). gandha = scent/perfume (alternative: fragrant substances). danta = tusk (alternative: ivory).

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: "No," says Kautilya.
notes: na-iti is an unsandhied join of two words; glossary formula.

words.gloss: with the wares of blankets, hides and horses excluded
wares of conch, diamond, gem, pearl, gold

hindi: कम्बल, खाल और घोड़े के पण्य को छोड़े हुए, और शंख, वज्र, मणि, मोती, सोने के पण्य दक्षिणापथ में अधिक प्रचुर हैं।
english: [Wares] with the wares of blankets, hides and horses excluded, and the wares of conch, diamond, gem, pearl and gold, [are] more abundant in the southern route.
notes: The syntax of varjāḥ with ca is unclear. The usual reading is 'excepting the wares of blankets, hides and horses, the wares of conch, diamond, gem, pearl and gold are more abundant in the southern route'; here the words are rendered literally and the connection of the two nominatives by ca is kept. prabhūtatarā = prabhūtatarāḥ (visarga dropped before d). Low confidence on the construction.

hindi: दक्षिणापथ में भी बहुत खानों वाला, बहुमूल्य पण्य वाला, प्रसिद्ध गति वाला, अथवा थोड़े व्यय और व्यायाम वाला वणिक्-पथ बेहतर, अथवा प्रचुर देश वाला, तुच्छ पण्य वाला।
english: In the southern route too, the merchant route with many mines, valuable wares, a well-known course, or little expenditure and exertion, [is] better; or [the one] with extensive territory [and] insignificant wares.

text_flags.why: possible: puṇya (merit) for paṇya (wares), as in the preceding paṇya compounds and the contrast with sāra.paṇyaḥ; the e-text also has sāra.phalgu.puṇyānāṃ in 2.35

notes: The second vā is unclear: it may offer a further alternative or contrast the route 'with extensive territory but insignificant wares' as the lesser one (then 'than' would be needed); rendered literally. viṣaya = territory. phalgu = insignificant (glossary 3.17). If the printed puṇya is kept it would read 'with insignificant merit', not a sense that fits.

hindi: इससे पूर्व और पश्चिम वणिक्-पथ की व्याख्या की गई।
english: By that the eastern and the western merchant route are explained.
notes: vyākhyātaḥ is singular although there are two subjects (glossary 4.4). pūrva = eastern (alternative: former), contrasted with paścima 'western'.

words.gloss: of wheel route and foot route
because of being of vast undertaking
with feasibility of place and time

hindi: वहाँ भी चक्र-मार्ग और पाद-मार्ग में चक्र-मार्ग विपुल आरम्भ वाला होने के कारण बेहतर, अथवा देश-काल की सम्भावना वाला गधे-ऊँट का मार्ग।
english: There too, of the wheel route and the foot route, the wheel route [is] better because of [its] vast undertaking, or the donkey-camel route, with feasibility of place and time.
notes: sambhāvana is uncertain (feasibility, probability, supposition); 'feasibility' is a tentative literal choice and the exact relation (depending on place and time) is not applied. The construction after vā (donkey-camel route [is better]) is understood.

hindi: इन दोनों से अंस-पथ की व्याख्या की गई।
english: By these two the shoulder route is explained.
notes: aṃsa = shoulder (the route of porters carrying on the shoulder is an interpretation, not stated).

hindi: दूसरे के कर्म का उदय नेता का क्षय है; विपरीत में वृद्धि।
english: The rise of the other's works [is] the leader's decline; in the reverse [case], growth.
notes: GROUPING: units 29 and 30 are the two halves of one verse (the sentence continues in unit 30). para = the other (glossary 9.2), not 'enemy'; karma = works (glossary 7.1 sva-karma / para-karma, the king's own and the other's undertakings). netṛ = leader (the conqueror of the next unit is meant, not stated). kṣaya/vṛddhi = decline/growth.

hindi: समान कर्म-पथ में विजिगीषु द्वारा अपना स्थान जाना जाना चाहिए।
english: In an equal course of works, own stagnation is to be known by the conqueror.
notes: GROUPING: second half of the verse begun in unit 29. sthāna = stagnation (glossary 9.7, 7.1), Hindi स्थान by the glossary (reads as 'place' otherwise). Equal (tulye) = when the other's action and one's own course are equal, not stated.

words.gloss: having little income and excessive expenditure

hindi: थोड़ी आय और अत्यधिक व्यय वाला होना क्षय है; विपरीत में वृद्धि।
english: Having little income and excessive expenditure [is] decline; in the reverse [case], growth.
notes: GROUPING: units 31 and 32 are the two halves of one verse. āgama = income (arrival). The compound is read as alpa-āgama + ati-vyaya + tā.

hindi: आय और व्यय की समानता स्थान है, कर्मों में अपने का जानने योग्य।
english: Equal income and expenditure [is] stagnation of oneself, to be known in works.
notes: GROUPING: second half of the verse begun in unit 31. samāya is read sama-āya ('equal income'); the alternative is sam-āya. ātmanaḥ may qualify sthānam ('stagnation of oneself', as rendered) or jñeyam; cf. unit 30 'svaṃ sthānam'. Hindi अपने का is deliberately literal.

hindi: “इसलिए जिसके आरम्भ में थोड़ा व्यय है, जिसका महान् उदय है, दुर्ग आदि में —
english: "Therefore, [that] whose undertaking has little expenditure, [and] of great rise, in forts and the rest —
notes: GROUPING: units 33 and 34 are the two halves of one verse; the sentence continues in unit 34, where the noun karma 'work' completes it ('having obtained work ...'). The unit is a fragment of adjectives, accusative singular neuter, agreeing with karma of unit 34; the Hindi ends open with a dash.

hindi: कर्म पाकर श्रेष्ठ हो जाए,” ऐसी कर्म-सन्धियाँ कही गई हैं।
english: having obtained works, [one] would be superior," — such are the treaties of works stated.
notes: GROUPING: second half of the verse begun in unit 33; the quotation (here treated as running from the start of unit 33, which has no mark) is closed by iti. karma = works (the undertaking acquired), as in karma-sandhi of unit 1 and glossary 7.1/7.3; singular rendered 'works' as the glossary term. In units 11-12 (conduct of troops, discipline) karma stays 'action'. uktāḥ is a participle in agreement with karma-sandhayaḥ (m. nom. pl.).
